message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) depending on the exact route you take. On a clear day, with normal traffic and staying within speed‑limit limits, you can expect the trip to take around **6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic can be heavy, add an extra hour or two. Conversely, if you’re traveling on a quiet weekday morning or evening, you might shave off a bit of time.  

A quick way to get a more precise estimate is to plug your departure time into a navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps, etc.) – they’ll factor in real‑time traffic and give you a dynamic ETA.
